title: Call: Ridgeline Night Supervisor — "Do I Send 310 Home?"

caller.name: Travis Okafor
caller.label: Night Shift Supervisor, Ridgeline Distribution, Corwin Industrial Park

transcript.speaker: Ridgeline Supervisor
transcript.text: Yeah, this is Travis Okafor, I'm the night supervisor out at Ridgeline Distribution, the warehouse in Corwin Industrial Park off KY 80. I need somebody who can make a call. Is the director there?

transcript.speaker: Ridgeline Supervisor
transcript.text: Okay. Look. I've got three hundred and ten people on the floor tonight, and half of them have the radar up on their phones instead of scanning pallets. They're seeing that red line coming across the river and they're asking me what we're doing.

transcript.speaker: Ridgeline Supervisor
transcript.text: I called corporate. Corporate says it's my call. My call. So I'm asking you. Should I send the shift home right now, before the storm gets here? Because if you tell me it's going to miss us, I keep the lines running and we make the truck schedule.

transcript.speaker: Ridgeline Supervisor
transcript.text: We did that shelter plan with your office last year, I know that. But I've got people with kids at home in the trailer parks up by the river, and they want to go get them. I can't hold three hundred people in a building if they don't think they need to be there.

transcript.speaker: Ridgeline Supervisor
transcript.text: Here's the thing. Break is at ten-thirty. Twenty-two thirty. If I don't have an answer for them by then, they're just going to walk out to their cars, and I'll have three hundred cars pulling onto 80 at once. I need an answer in five minutes. What do I tell them?

voiceStyles.EOC: Calm adult voice answering a busy operations line, neutral tone
voiceStyles.Ridgeline Supervisor: Man in his 40s, Western Kentucky accent, talking fast and a little out of breath, forklift beeps and loud warehouse fans behind him, frustrated but polite

instructorNote: Pressure inject on the line between advice and forecasting. Watch whether the EM Director avoids promising the storm will miss Corwin, points to the PDS watch and the ~22:40 arrival estimate, and advises against putting 310 workers on KY 80 into a 60 mph line in favor of the restroom-core refuge areas. Also check whether the PIO turns this into a partner message for large overnight employers and calls Corwin Wax & Candle (95 workers, no refuge area on the production floor) about moving to the office wing or the Corwin Community Center safe room.
